chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام: the maximum that menstruation may be is eight, and the minimum that it may be is three.

This report does not contradict the reports we have presented, due to the consensus of the sect being contrary to it, and because none of our companions held that the furthest limit of the days of menstruation is less than ten days. Even if it were accepted, it would be possible for us to interpret it as referring to a woman whose habit was eight days, then she became in a state of istiḥāḍah; for the most that is obligatory upon her is that she leave salat (prayer) during the days of her habit, and that is eight days, as we explained in Kitāb Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām.

key_terms.أَدْنَى: the minimum limit in legal duration
key_terms.أَكْثَرَ: the maximum limit in legal duration
key_terms.إِجْمَاعِ: consensus; the agreement of the Shia scholars cited as evidence
key_terms.اسْتُحِيضَتْ: she experienced istiḥāḍah, irregular non-menstrual bleeding
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: salat (prayer), which is left during the established menstrual period
key_terms.الْحَيْضُ: menstruation; the legal state and period under discussion
key_terms.تَهْذِيبِ الْأَحْكَامِ: Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām, the work referenced for further explanation

ai.seo_question: How does al-Istibṣār reconcile a hadith stating that the maximum menstruation is eight days with the ruling of ten days?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the legal ruling on the minimum and maximum duration of menstruation in Shia fiqh. Although one report states that the maximum is eight days, the text explains that this does not oppose the established reports and consensus that set the upper limit at ten days, and it may be interpreted as referring to a woman whose normal habit was eight days followed by istiḥāḍah.
